sanskrit: सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसंभवाः । निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम् ॥
hindiTranslation: हे महाबाहो  प्रकृतिसे उत्पन्न होनेवाले सत्त्व, रज और तम  ये तीनों गुण अविनाशी देहीको देहमें बाँध देते हैं ॥
englishTranslation: Arjuna, the three qualities of nature—sattva, rajas, and tamas—bind the imperishable inner being to the body.
essence: Nature's three forces keep the changeless one identified with the body.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: The three qualities born from nature keep the imperishable inner being tied to the body.
simpleInsight: You are not trapped by weakness alone; the whole system of nature can keep you identified.
detailedMeaning: Krishna explains why beings stay caught in embodied life. Sattva, rajas, and tamas are forces of nature, and they bind the unchanging inner being to the body.
modernRelevance: You promise yourself to stay calm at a family dinner, then irritation or fog takes over anyway. Krishna names the three forces behind that pull, so you can see them working instead of only blaming yourself.
translationLiteral: सत्त्वं (sattva) / रजः (rajas) / तमः (tamas) / इति (thus) / गुणाः (qualities) / प्रकृतिसंभवाः (born of nature) / निबध्नन्ति (bind) / महाबाहो (mighty-armed one) / देहे (in the body) / देहिनम् (the embodied one) / अव्ययम् (imperishable)
insight: Sattva, rajas and tamas all bind the deathless self to the body; none of the three sets it free.
